title: The overnight Oh Happy Day album and moves to Dunhill, ABC and Motown
summary: Lee produced a ten-song gospel album with Oh Happy Day in a weekend for Dunhill, then moved to ABC in 1969 and Motown in 1973 and again in 1977.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But a record came out, "Oh Happy Day" at the time, and so Jay [Flasko] over at Dunhill, he's a great marketing man, and so he saw the marketing people that were doing this record had slipped up on something, and so he called me on a Friday and told me he wanted an album on the street by Monday and could I do it.

He wanted 10 religious songs, but he wanted "Oh Happy Day" in it, and he said he had the cover ready, and could I get the record. And I had him hold on the phone and I got in touch -- incidentally, the young man works here now, James Carmichael, who produces the Commodores -- well, James Carmichael and another fellow named Arthur Wright who is now producing the Pips, well I called both of them -- they were both pretty heavy in to the church, and I told him what we wanted to do, and did they think we could pull it off. And they said yes.

So I used 10 musicians and about 35 singers, and we went to Radio Recorders, and one would rehearse the singers and the other would rehearse the band. And I had 3 copies over in the corner; they were copying the music as we did it. And now what he had detected, that they had Edwin Hawkins -- it said the Edwin Hawkins Singers on their album; you know, the people who did "Oh Happy Day" -- so all he had on his was "Oh Happy Day".
So anyway, to make a long story short, we got it

out; I had it on his desk Monday morning, and he got the album and they put it all over Wallach's Music City, in the window, and see, people were buying "Oh Happy Day". They would go in and say, "Give me Oh Happy Day". So they didn't know who the guy was, you know, and on the one that I did, I had a woman singing it, and that's how I left UA to go to Dunhill Records. Because I told him that -- I said, "Well, doing this for you and working for another record company, I may lose my gig." He said, "If you lose your gig, come to me."
And so I prevaricated and told them they were giving me a lot of heat, and so I went over -- because I wanted to change jobs. And that's how I went over to ABC.

In '69. And I stayed until '73, and in June, I came to Motown, and in '73, and I stayed at Motown I was always the head of A & R. 7 weeks, and went back to ABC. And then last January 15, 1977, I came back to Motown. Now don't be surprised in 1978 I go back to ABC.
